🔊 Pezeshkian says he will convey Iranian nation’s grievances, strength to world

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian, who has left Tehran for New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), says he will use the session to convey to officials and people from around the world the grievances and injustices suffered by the Iranian nation as a result of foreign pressure.

Pezeshkian made the remarks before departing Tehran on Tuesday morning, local time.
​
He said some countries use their power to bully others and violate the rights of other nations. “The UN General Assembly is a platform where we can make our positions, our grievances, and our strength heard by the world,” he said.
​
The president said he would use the General Assembly session, as well as meetings with media and cultural figures and talks with senior officials, to outline Iran’s positions and convey the strength of the Iranian people.
​
He said he would also highlight crimes committed by Iran’s enemies against the Iranian people and the mistrust they have created.
​
“We have been at the negotiating table several times and signed an agreement. They [enemies] acted against the negotiations and understandings reached. The world has seen and continues to see that they have easily violated those understandings,” Pezeshkian said, referring to the two wars waged by the United States and Israel against Iran in 2025 and 2026 amid negotiations between Tehran and Washington. The United States also abandoned a memorandum reached with Iran in mid-June this year, less than a month after it was signed.
​
Pezeshkian stressed that peace cannot prevail in the world unless the rights of nations are respected, saying that no one can force others into submission through coercion.
​
He also said enemies continue to kill civilians and attack civilian sites in Yemen, Palestine, Syria, and Iran under the pretext of fighting terrorism.
​
“Were the innocent children of Minab and Lamerd terrorists? Do attacks on homes and hospitals constitute fighting terrorism?” Pezeshkian said, referring to US-Israeli airstrikes on the Iranian cities of Minab and Lamerd in February, in which children were among those killed.
​
“It is actions that speak to the facts, not words,” he said.
​
Referring to the US refusal to issue visas to members of his media team, Pezeshkian said the measure shows that Washington is concerned about its actions being brought to the world’s attention.
​
“They are trying to prevent the voice of the Iranian people from being heard and have blocked the presence of Iran’s media delegation. However, many international media outlets are present, and if we manage our message effectively, we will be able to make the voice of the Iranian people heard,” he said.
​
Concluding his remarks, Pezeshkian said the adversaries had failed to achieve their objectives through military action and had now resorted to other measures, including disrupting air and land routes and fomenting internal divisions, in an attempt to force the Iranian nation to surrender.
​
He added that the Iranian people would once again thwart their adversaries’ efforts through unity and under the leadership of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution.

📲 @Irna_en​
